newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices firm on storage demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices firm on storage demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices firmed several cents Monday despite relatively mild U.S. weather, boosted by stepped up storage demand, traders said.

With almost no extreme heat expected in the U.S. this week, traders said storage operators, still short gas and eyeing favorable autumn-to-winter price spreads, were opting to pick up the pace of injections.

"The cash is short and prices have been strong because of storage buying," said one East Coast trader, noting swing prices on Gulf pipes firmed a few cents from Friday to the mid-to-high $1.80s, up almost 10 cents from September indices.

Traders said current Gulf cash prices, nearly 40 cents below December NYMEX, offered operators, particularly in the producing region, an economic incentive to stock build. But some said strong buying now may haunt the cash later.
"Injection demand may prop up the fronts, but longer-term, it will be bearish," said one Houston-based trader.
Midcontinent prices scored similar gains for the day to about the $1.70 level, also several cents over index.
In west Texas, prices on El Paso Permian were up three to four cents to the low-$1.60sf, about even with Sept 1 levels.
In the Northeast, gas at the New York city gate was quoted little changed in the low-$2s.
-- J Silha, New York Power Desk 212-859-1624
